approved: Excise Tariff Amendment (Carbon Tax Repeal) Bill 2014
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is part of a package that would repeal the carbon tax.
The package would ban businesses from price exploitation on key goods like electricity and gas after the repeal, and give the ACCC powers to monitor prices.
A corporation that breaches the ban could face a maximum penalty of 6,471 penalty units, and an individual 1,295 penalty units.
Introduces a new prohibition on price exploitation for certain key goods related to the carbon tax repeal.
Gives the ACCC monitoring powers to assess the effect of the carbon tax repeal on prices.
Introduces a new prohibition on false or misleading representations about the carbon tax repeal's effect on prices.
Businesses supplying key goods such as electricity and gas, and consumers.

Moved a debate management motion to fast-track passage of the carbon tax repeal bills through the House together, arguing the September 2013 election gave the coalition a clear mandate, and recalled the 2010 pledge that there would be no carbon tax under a government Julia Gillard led.

Moved the second reading of the carbon tax repeal bills, saying Treasury modelling shows households will save an average of $550 a year, that the tax has cost $15 billion over two years, and citing an Independent Competition and Regulatory Commission estimate that electricity prices in the ACT will fall by 11.6 per cent once it is repealed.
Excise Tariff Amendment (Carbon Tax Repeal) Act 2014
